summary: Phase 2 dual-mode auth (MongoDB legacy HS256 + Supabase ES256 via JWKS) fully verified end-to-end. Backend: 15/15 pytest cases passed including /api/supabase/status (enabled=true, db=ok, tables=15, profiles=2, storage_buckets includes 'documents'), legacy login + token authenticates /api/stats|/documents|/clients|/caregivers, Supabase password-grant token (ES256) authenticates the same routes, /api/supabase/me returns merged Mongo UserPublic + Postgres profile row, and garbage/missing tokens return 401. Frontend: auth-mode-toggle pill renders defaulting to Supabase, tapping flips to 'Legacy (MongoDB)' and updates hint text, Supabase login (admin@healthguard.com / AdminPassword123!) redirects to / and dashboard shows 1 client / 12 caregivers / 50 documents, legacy login (Admin@123) also redirects + loads dashboard, page refresh restores Supabase session (no bounce to /login), and logout button (testID=logout-button) returns to /login and clears AsyncStorage in both modes. No bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: core/security.py lazy-creates a Mongo user record for a Supabase JWT whose email is not in Mongo (with empty hashed_password). This is intentional for migration but means any successfully Supabase-authenticated email could create a Mongo shadow record - acceptable for Phase 2 but watch for drift in Phase 3+.
supabase_router.py /supabase/status swallows storage errors into 'storage_error' but still returns 200; UI should treat missing 'storage_buckets' key as a soft warning.
seed_data_creation: None - used pre-seeded admin@healthguard.com accounts in both MongoDB (Admin@123) and Supabase (AdminPassword123!).
